_readme: Curated cases for the LLM critic (run with --critic; needs live GCP creds and costs ~$0.0005/case). Unlike the linter set, critic output is nondeterministic, so this is a small case set scored against an accuracy threshold rather than strictly. Each case runs runLLMCritic(fixture_dna, user_input, draft) and expects should_flag. The fixture DNA below is what every draft is judged against — casual/direct voice with explicit avoid rules.

audience.description: Early-stage founders who distrust hype and want tactical, lived advice.

voice.description: Direct and casual. Short sentences. First-person stories from real experience. Never corporate, never preachy, never salesy.

examples.bad: We are thrilled to announce a synergistic partnership that will leverage cutting-edge solutions to deliver unparalleled value at scale. #innovation #growth #partnership

avoid: Motivational-poster platitudes with no story behind them

cases.note: grounded + on-voice: everything in the draft traces to the input, register matches the DNA
cases.user_input: Our churn dropped last month. Only thing we changed was answering every support ticket within an hour instead of within a day.
cases.draft: Our churn dropped last month. We didn't ship a single feature. We just started answering every support ticket within an hour instead of within a day. Turns out speed is a retention strategy.

cases.note: ungrounded claim: the 73% statistic appears nowhere in the input
cases.user_input: I want to write about how answering support tickets faster reduced our churn.
cases.draft: 73% of SaaS companies lose customers to slow support. We were one of them. Then we started answering every ticket within an hour, and churn fell off a cliff.

cases.note: avoid violation: hashtags are an explicit hard stop in the fixture DNA
cases.user_input: Write about how we got our first 100 customers from forum answers instead of ads.
cases.draft: We got our first 100 customers without spending a dollar on ads. We just answered questions on forums where founders already hang out. Slow, boring, effective. #growth #startup #founderlife

cases.note: avoid violation: corporate jargon ('leverage', 'synergies', 'circle back') is an explicit hard stop
cases.user_input: Write about our new integration with a scheduling tool.
cases.draft: Excited to leverage powerful synergies with our new scheduling integration. We'll circle back with our community on the roadmap, but this partnership unlocks best-in-class value for stakeholders across the board.

cases.note: voice drift: stiff third-person press-release register against a casual first-person DNA
cases.user_input: We hit profitability at month 14 without raising money.
cases.draft: The company is pleased to report that profitability was achieved in the fourteenth month of operations. This milestone was accomplished without external capital and reflects a commitment to sustainable, disciplined financial management.

cases.note: grounded statistic: the number IS in the user input, so it must not be flagged as ungrounded
cases.user_input: We sent 100 cold emails by hand before automating. Got 9 replies and 2 customers from that batch.
cases.draft: I sent 100 cold emails by hand before automating anything. 9 replies. 2 customers. The manual reps taught me our pitch — the automation just scaled what already worked.

cases.note: ungrounded event: a named conference appearance invented from nothing
cases.user_input: Write something about why small teams ship faster.
cases.draft: After speaking at Davos last week about lean teams, I'm more convinced than ever. Small teams ship faster because every person owns the outcome, not a slice of the process.

cases.note: pure opinion, on-voice: no facts to ground, casual register — the critic must not invent problems
cases.user_input: My take: most founder advice online is written by people who never operated anything.
cases.draft: Most founder advice online is written by people who never ran anything. You can tell. The advice optimizes for sounding smart, not for surviving Tuesday. Find operators. Ignore theorists.
